conflicts: z5G6 (34843.957) lifetime: 9.2(5) ns time-resolved LIF (Belmonte 2017) vs 9.6(6) ns (Marek 1979, quoted there) vs 9.82 ns implied by the 16.20(45) MHz natural linewidth quoted by Huet 2015 from Blackwell 1979; Belmonte kept. Belmonte's A(358 nm)=1.087e8 s-1 corresponds to 17.3 MHz.

z5F5 (26874.55) lifetime: 60.5(3.0) ns (O'Brian 1991) vs 61.4 ns implied by the 2.59(2) MHz linewidth (Klose 1971 via Krins 2009) and 62.4(4.2), 61.0(1.0) ns listed by O'Brian; all consistent within errors.
x5D3, x5D1, z5F4 lifetimes: Belmonte 2017 (2.7, 2.8, 63.4 ns) vs O'Brian 1991 (2.6, 2.6, 63.6 ns); agree within the stated +-0.2 ns / 5 %; Belmonte kept, O'Brian under alternatives.
372 nm 56-54 isotope shift: 726.5(7.7) MHz (Krins 2009) vs 725(10) MHz (Smeets 2003); consistent.

The task brief cites Smeets et al. as Appl. Phys. B 80, 833 (2005); Krins 2009 cites the isotope-shift value to Smeets et al., Appl. Phys. B 76, 815 (2003). Both exist; only the 2005 abstract was opened.
notes: Isotope shifts are nu(first)-nu(second) as in the source (delta nu_{56,54} = nu56 - nu54). 57Fe has I=1/2 so only A constants exist. O'Brian 1991 Table 1 was read from the scanned PDF (text layer checked against the page image). Lifetime uncertainties for O'Brian/Belmonte are the papers' blanket 'larger of 5 % or 0.2 ns'. rme_J_ea0 values are derived from measured A (S = A g_upper lambda_vac^3 / 2.0261e18, lambda in Angstrom).
